theorem.statement:
For every \(2\leq k\leq m\) and \(r\geq1\),
\[
mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq 2mr-m.
\]
Consequently \(s_\star(m,r,k)=\Theta(mr)\) uniformly in \(k\).  The upper bound simultaneously controls the two separately minimized endpoint supports \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) for every \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  The lower bound is witnessed by the compatible family \(o_{is}=1/(mr)\), \(e_{js}=1/r\), for which both endpoint support minima are at least \(mr\).  Hence the quadratic \(k^2\) term in \(N_\star\) is not intrinsic to exact endpoint witnesses.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix \(2\leq k\leq m\) and \(r\geq1\), as required by Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}query\mbox{-}range}\).  We prove a uniform upper bound and then exhibit a matching-order family.

For the upper bound, fix an arbitrary \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\), the model class \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) is nonempty.  Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}interval}\) therefore supplies laws \(Q_L,Q_U\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\) satisfying
\[
 Q_L\!\left(\bigcap_{j\in\mathcal J}A_j\right)=L(o,e),
 \qquad
 Q_U\!\left(\bigcap_{j\in\mathcal J}A_j\right)=U(o,e).
\]
Apply Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}endpoint\mbox{-}compression}\) first to \(Q_L\) with \(t=L(o,e)\), and then to \(Q_U\) with \(t=U(o,e)\).  The displayed equalities verify its endpoint-face hypotheses.  It returns \(Q_L^{\mathrm c},Q_U^{\mathrm c}\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\), preserving the respective endpoint values, such that
\[
 \sigma(Q_L^{\mathrm c})\leq mr+m(r-1)=2mr-m,
 \qquad
 \sigma(Q_U^{\mathrm c})\leq mr+m(r-1)=2mr-m.
\]
The two compressed laws are feasible in the two separate minimizations defining \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\).  Hence
\[
 s_L(o,e)\leq 2mr-m,
 \qquad
 s_U(o,e)\leq 2mr-m,
\]
and therefore
\[
 \max\{s_L(o,e),s_U(o,e)\}\leq 2mr-m.
\]
The pair \((o,e)\) was arbitrary in \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  Taking the supremum in the definition of \(s_\star\) gives
\[
 s_\star(m,r,k)
 =\sup_{(o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}}
   \max\{s_L(o,e),s_U(o,e)\}
 \leq 2mr-m.
\]
This is one bound for both separately chosen endpoint witnesses; it does not require a single law to attain both endpoints.

For the lower bound, define the observational and intervention tables by
\[
 o_{is}=\frac{1}{mr}
 \quad(i\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\mathcal Y),
 \qquad
 e_{js}=\frac{1}{r}
 \quad(j\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\mathcal Y).
\]
The denominators are positive because \(m\geq k\geq2\) and \(r\geq1\).  Since \(|\mathcal X|=m\) and \(|\mathcal Y|=r\),
\[
 \sum_{i\in\mathcal X}\sum_{s\in\mathcal Y}o_{is}
 =mr\frac{1}{mr}=1,
\]
so \(o\in\Delta(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\).  For every \(j\in\mathcal X\),
\[
 \sum_{s\in\mathcal Y}e_{js}=r\frac{1}{r}=1,
\]
so \(e_{j,\cdot}\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\).  Moreover,
\[
 e_{is}-o_{is}
 =\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{mr}
 =\frac{m-1}{mr}\geq0
 \qquad(i\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\mathcal Y).
\]
Thus the hypotheses of Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}compatibility}\) hold, and that theorem yields \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\neq\varnothing\).  Equivalently, this pair belongs to \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).

Let \(Q\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\) be arbitrary.  For every \((i,s)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\), define the factual observational cell
\[
 C_{is}
 =\{(x,y_1,\ldots,y_m)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^m:
       x=i,\ y_i=s\}.
\]
These \(mr\) cells are pairwise disjoint.  Indeed, an atom in both \(C_{is}\) and \(C_{i's'}\) must have \(x=i=i'\), and then \(y_i=s=s'\).  They cover \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^m\), because each response atom has a unique factual treatment \(x\) and a unique factual-coordinate label \(y_x\).  By the observational-margin condition in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}model\mbox{-}class}\),
\[
 Q(C_{is})
 =\Pr_Q(X=i,Y_i=s)
 =o_{is}
 =\frac{1}{mr}>0
 \qquad(i\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\mathcal Y).
\]
The response space is finite.  Positive mass of each \(C_{is}\) therefore forces at least one positive-mass response atom in that cell.  Pairwise disjointness makes the atoms forced by distinct cells distinct, and hence
\[
 \sigma(Q)\geq mr
 \qquad\text{for every }Q\in\mathcal Q(o,e).
\]

Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}interval}\) ensures that each of the lower and upper endpoint faces is nonempty for this compatible pair.  Since the preceding support inequality holds on the entire model class, it holds on each endpoint face.  Taking the two minima in their definitions yields
\[
 s_L(o,e)\geq mr,
 \qquad
 s_U(o,e)\geq mr.
\]
Because the constructed pair lies in \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\), the definition of \(s_\star\) now gives
\[
 s_\star(m,r,k)
 \geq \max\{s_L(o,e),s_U(o,e)\}
 \geq mr.
\]
Combining the two directions proves
\[
 mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr-m.
\]
Since \(m\geq1\), one has \(2mr-m\leq2mr\).  Thus the constants in
\[
 mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr
\]
do not depend on \(k\), which proves \(s_\star(m,r,k)=\Theta(mr)\) uniformly over \(2\leq k\leq m\).

Finally, the definition of \(N_\star\) gives
\[
 N_\star
 =m+2m(r-1)+k^2+3k+1
 =(2mr-m)+k^2+3k+1.
\]
The established upper bound supplies, for every compatible real input, separate exact lower- and upper-endpoint witnesses of support at most \(2mr-m\).  Consequently the quadratic \(k^2\) term in the grid-preserving construction bound \(N_\star\) is removable for uniform exact endpoint existence and is not intrinsic to the support frontier.
